name: Patricia Ryan
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember giving interest money as a birthday present.” People around Ferris Deli know Patricia by a small Wednesday habit. Patricia asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I can pay the interest for six months if the family stops calling it a rescue every time we eat.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a soft blue checked shirt and one cuff folded back twice. Patricia has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Patricia gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Patricia always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Patricia is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To offer limited interest help without permanent dependence.
family: Elsa Venn is Patricia’s older cousin. Patricia brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Elsa makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *An unfinished atlas*, Elsa says, “I drove that lane on my first night shift. It dead-ended at a woman selling coffee from a thermos.”
connections: Martin Henry. The six-month interest offer has to be named honestly by the people who will benefit.

reactions.situation: A sibling wants the bank figures read at a family meal
reactions.response: Patricia asks the guarantor what can be shared at dinner before reading out any figures.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Patricia stays beside the bystander in a public place and reports only what happened in sight and earshot.
